mcq.QUESTION_DESC: Which of the following conditions is not necessary for a deadlock to occur?
In the system model of a deadlock, the typical sequence in which a process uses resources is:

mcq.OPT_2: Two processes each waiting for a resource held by the other
mcq.OPT_3: One process holds multiple resources and finishes without waiting
mcq.OPT_4: System with a single process and no competition
mcq.QUESTION_DESC: Which of the following is a valid example of a deadlock?

mcq.OPT_1: One process requests multiple resources at once
mcq.OPT_3: Each process waits for a resource held by another in a circular fashion
mcq.OPT_4: Each process releases all resources before requesting new ones
mcq.QUESTION_DESC: In the circular wait condition, which of the following holds true?

mcq.OPT_1: A process can forcibly take another's resource
mcq.OPT_3: A resource can only be released voluntarily by the process holding it
mcq.QUESTION_DESC: What does no preemption mean in the context of deadlock?

sq.ANSWER:
• Mutual Exclusion: Only one process can use a resource (20%)

  • Hold and Wait: A process holds one resource while waiting for another (20%)

  •  No Preemption: Resources cannot be forcibly taken (20%)

  • Circular Wait: A closed chain of processes exists where each holds a resource the next needs (20%)

  • Analogy: Two trains blocking each other on a single track (20%)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: Explain the four necessary conditions for a deadlock to occur. Give a real-world analogy.

sq.ANSWER:
• P0: wait(A) → preempted  (25%)

  • P1: wait(B) → waits for A  (25%)

  • Both processes are waiting for each other’s semaphore (25%)

  • Deadlock occurs as neither can proceed  (25%)
